title: Set the RL time constant to 1 ms
story: A 10 V step drives a 100 mH coil in series with a resistor. The current, and so the voltage across the resistor, must rise to 63.2 % of its final value (6.32 V) in about 1 ms, and be fully settled (above 9.5 V) well before 6 ms. Pick the resistor that sets tau = L / R to 1 ms.

goals.label: resistor voltage reaches 6.32 V between 0.8 and 1.2 ms

hints: tau = L / R. With L = 0.1 H, which R gives 0.001 s?
A bigger resistor makes the RL circuit faster, the opposite of an RC circuit.
